No new statistics this week. Instead, we take the tools you already have (`count()`, `prop.test()`, `bayes_prop_test()`, `t.test()`) and run them on real data from across criminal justice: reentry, pretrial release, neighborhoods, police use of force, risk assessment, and police stops. Every question runs the same four-step recipe, so by the end of the night the steps should feel routine. Then we look at what data is out there, because this is the week you choose the dataset for your final project.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this week you can:

- take a two-group question about a dataset you have never seen and choose the right test: `prop.test()` (and `bayes_prop_test()`) for a yes/no outcome, `t.test()` for a number
- say what a result means: the honest sentence, how big in real units, and one thing the test cannot tell you
- use `filter()` to compare like with like when two groups differ in more than one way
- size up a new dataset quickly (what one row is, how many rows, what the variables are, anything strange) and choose one for your final project

## Before class

- **No new reading.** Use the breathing room to catch up if you're behind
- Glance at the **[Final-Project Data Options](../project-data.qmd)** page so the datasets are not brand new when we tour them
- Bring your laptop. Nothing to install: every dataset tonight loads with `read_csv()`

## In class

- The recipe, used all night: **question** (two groups, one outcome) → **count or describe** → **test** → **say it** (the sentence, the size, what it cannot tell you)
- Four worked examples, each with an animation you can replay on the demo page:
  - **Reentry:** did financial aid at release lower re-arrest? (p = 0.063, and a 97% probability it did; the animation shows what that p-value is measuring)
  - **Pretrial release:** were employed arrestees released more often, and does the gap survive comparing people with the same record?
  - **Neighborhoods:** how much lower is income in Chicago's high-violence community areas, in dollars?
  - **Use of force:** was body camera footage reported more often in fatal police shootings after 2020?
- **Lab 7:** two more, and you write the code. A pretrial risk-assessment tool with me, then Minneapolis police stops on your own ([lab page](../labs/lab-07-workshop.qmd)). You submit your Your Turn script
- **What's out there:** a tour of the [data options](../project-data.qmd), how to size up a dataset in five minutes, and two ways to load one

*Missed class? The [demo walkthrough](../demos/demo-07-workshop.qmd) reproduces all four lecture examples step by step.*
